en.title: Number of Contiguous Rank Groups for Each Integer Mean
en.description:
The array is a permutation of 1..n. For each x=1..n, find the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays whose average is exactly x. Different index ranges are counted separately.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains n distinct ranks. The original bounds are 1≤n≤1000, and the array is exactly a permutation of 1..n, not a general array with duplicate values.
en.output: Output n integers; the x-th is the number of ranges whose mean is x.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 1 2 3 2 1; 1 2 2 1; and 1 1 1 4 4 1 1, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Enumerate the left and right endpoints and extend the range sum incrementally; whenever the sum is divisible by the length, add 1 to the count of the corresponding mean.
